'''Nicholas John Turner''', {{postnom|country=GBR|FRS}} is a British [[chemist]] and a professor in the [[Department of Chemistry, University of Manchester|Department of Chemistry]] at [[University of Manchester|The University of Manchester]].<ref name="D1"/> His research in general is based on [[biochemistry]] and [[organic chemistry]], specifically on [[biotechnology]], [[cell biology]], [[biocatalysis]] and [[organic synthesis]].<ref name="googles"/><ref name="Publi"/>

== Education ==
From the age of 13 (after attending an unknown preparatory school), Turner attended [[Preston School]] in Somerset, UK. Turner completed his Bachelor of Science degree in [[Chemistry]] in 1982 at [[University of Bristol]].<ref name="D1"/> He then read for his Doctor of Philosophy degree at [[University of Oxford]] on ''Mechanistic studies on isopenicillin N synthase'' and successfully completed it in 1985.<ref name="Research" /> His PhD was supervised by  [[Jack Baldwin (chemist)|Jack Baldwin]].<ref name="Research" />

== Research and career ==

Upon completing his PhD, Turner spent two years (1985–1987) with [[George M. Whitesides]] at [[Harvard University]] as a [[Royal Society]] Junior Research Fellow.<ref name="D1" /><ref name="D2" /> He then moved to [[University of Exeter]] as a lecturer in 1987, before moving to [[University of Edinburgh]] for the position of [[Reader (academic rank)|Reader]] in 1995.<ref name="D2" /> He was promoted to the position of Professor in 1998 and moved to [[University of Manchester]] as a professor of [[Chemical Biology]] in 2004.

Turner's research in general is based on [[biochemistry]] and [[organic chemistry]], specifically on [[biotechnology]], [[cell biology]], [[biocatalysis]] and [[organic synthesis]].<ref name="googles"/><ref name="Publi"/>

Turner is the Director of CoEBio<sup>3</sup>, an organisation designed to provide scientific environment in which the necessary research and development can be carried out to create new biocatalyst-based processes to meet the changing needs of industry in the next 10–20 years.<ref name="RSC1"/> He is also the co-founder of Ingenza and co-director of SYNBIOCHEM.<ref name="RSC2"/><ref name="RSC3"/> Turner is also the author of several books in the field of [[biocatalysis]] including ''Introduction to Biocatalysis Using Enzymes and Microorganisms'',<ref name="RSC4"/> and ''Biocatalysis in Organic Synthesis: The Retrosynthesis Approach''.<ref name="RSC5"/>

=== Notable work ===

Turner was elected as a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] in the year 2020.<ref name="Award6"/> Regarded one of the world's leading researchers<ref name="Award6"/> in the field of Biocatalysis, his profile reads:<blockquote>"Nicholas Turner undertakes research focussed on creating new enzymes for application as biocatalysts for chemical synthesis.<ref name="Mainresearch1" /><ref name="Mainresearch2" /><ref name="Mainresearch3" /> His group combine enzyme discovery with protein engineering and directed evolution methods in order to develop biocatalysts with tailored properties including high (stereo)selectivity, improved activity and enhanced stability. These biocatalysts, which include amine/alcohol oxidases, imine reductases, lyases, transaminases and monooxygenases, are then applied to the synthesis of a range of target molecules especially pharmaceuticals and fine chemicals.<ref name="Mainresearch4" /><ref name="Mainresearch5" /> ... Nick also has a passion for promoting the wider application of biocatalysis across the entire chemical community and has developed guidelines for 'biocatalytic retrosynthesis'<ref name="RSC5" /> to encourage greater adoption of biocatalysis amongst synthetic chemists."</blockquote>

=== Awards and nominations ===
* [[Royal Society of Chemistry|RSC]] Carbohydrate Chemistry Award (1992)<ref name=Award1/>
* [[Corday–Morgan Prize]] (1996)<ref name=Award2/>
* RSC Industrial Organic Award (2009)<ref name=Award3/> 
* Organic Stereochemistry Award (2017)<ref name=Award4/> 
* [[American Chemical Society|ACS]] Catalysis Lectureship (2018)<ref name=Award5/> 
* [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] (2020)<ref name=Award6/>
